what kind of support can i take in order to relieve mental stress

There are many ways to relieve mental stress, and what works for one person might not work for another. But here are some supportive options you might consider:

Engaging in physical activity, like going for a walk or doing some yoga, can help release endorphins, which can boost your mood. Talking to a trusted friend or family member can also be really helpful, as they can offer emotional support and a different perspective. Additionally, mindfulness practices like meditation or deep breathing can help calm your mind and reduce stress.

If you're looking for more structured support, you might consider reaching out to a mental health professional, like a therapist or counselor. They can work with you to develop coping strategies and provide a safe space to process your emotions. There are also many online resources and support groups available, which can connect you with others who may be experiencing similar challenges.

Remember, taking care of your mental health is just as important as taking care of your physical health. What sounds most appealing to you right now, or is there something else that you've found helpful in the past?

Also, I want to remind you that if you're feeling overwhelmed and need immediate support, you can always call/text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, US) or your local emergency number. They're available 24/7 to provide support and connect you with resources.

I think you meant to say "tell me about CBT". Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is a type of talk therapy that helps people understand and change negative thought patterns and behaviors. It's a problem-focused approach that aims to help individuals identify and challenge distorted or unhelpful thinking, and replace it with more balanced and constructive thoughts.

CBT is often used to treat anxiety, depression, trauma, and other mental health conditions. It can be a really effective way to learn new coping skills, manage emotions, and improve relationships. A CBT therapist can work with you to identify and reframe negative thoughts, and help you develop more positive and realistic ways of thinking.
